title: Constraint
description: A stated restriction on the solution space, such as a mandated or forbidden technology, a deadline, a budget ceiling, a jurisdiction or a contractual term, that limits which design or implementation options are permissible without describing a capability or quality the system must deliver. It is stated in decision records, policies or requirement text; code such as a fitness test may enforce it, but is not where it is defined. Use Requirement instead when the statement describes a function or quality the system must provide (what it must do or how well), rather than ruling options in or out for how it is built. Use Principle instead when the statement is a general normative rule meant to guide many decisions across systems (e.g. 'prefer managed services') rather than a specific, checkable limit on one solution. Use Driver instead when the item is the underlying condition or force (a new regulation, a market shift) that motivates change, rather than the concrete restriction derived from it. Use Assessment instead when the item is an analytical finding about the current state (a risk, gap or weakness) rather than a binding limit on design choices.

documentation.description: Free-text statement of the restriction, giving its source (regulation, contract, decision record, budget), the scope it applies to and how compliance can be checked; set it for every constraint so the limit can be verified.

constraintType.description: Category of constraint restricting the solution space

x-dr-evidence: An ADR or design doc section titled 'Constraints' or 'Decision drivers' with mandatory wording such as 'must use PostgreSQL 14', 'no GPL dependencies' or 'must ship before Q3'
Code comments or config justified by a cited rule, e.g. cloud region pinned to eu-* with a comment referencing GDPR data residency, or a deny-list of licences in a dependency-audit config

Architecture fitness tests or lint rules (ArchUnit, dependency-cruiser, import-linter) that forbid certain imports, libraries or runtime versions, together with documentation naming the restriction they enforce
